brief: Renewed US strikes on Iran pushed oil above $90/bbl for the first time since late July on fears of prolonged Strait of Hormuz disruption, compounding weak JOLTS, construction spending, manufacturing PMIs and Dallas Fed services data into stagflation fears. Refined-product prices (diesel, European natgas, heating oil) hit multi-year highs, which the note says should pressure headline inflation even if core impact stays uncertain, complicating a Fed considering another hike into a supply shock. Global sovereign yields reached their highest since 2008. Japan's 10Y topped 3% for the first time in 30 years. September rate-hike odds topped 70%. Nomura's McElligott warns that heavy demand for high-strike payers has left dealers short convexity, so a slow grind in yields turning into a jump could force a disorderly scramble to cover. Goldman's Privorotsky frames AI capex as both the equity bull case and the duration bear case, since AI investment and Treasury issuance compete for the same pool of savings, and he stays cautious on duration now that month-end support has passed. Stocks, gold and bitcoin all fell as the dollar strengthened.
